title: Bram and the Gravity
premise: Mara Amberdale, a xenolinguist haunted by dreams that no longer arrive in any human tongue, pilots the freighter Long Silence along a trade route between worlds that have stopped talking to each other during the Kess-Veyran war. When he intercepts a distress call in Ashkari—a language extinct for two hundred years—he realizes the message is not a plea for rescue but a treaty, recorded by survivors everyone believed dead, and both governments will kill to possess or bury it. Pursued by a Veyran hunter-ship and betrayed by the courier network he trusted, Mara gathers an unlikely crew of castoffs who become the family he never had, and learns the extinct language was preserved inside his own lost dreams: he is a descendant of the Ashkari diaspora, which is why he alone can verify the message's authenticity. In the end, Mara broadcasts the treaty from neutral ground at the cost of his ship and nearly his life, forcing both sides to the table—justice achieved outside any law, and an identity no longer hidden.
about_author: August Eriksen is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade transcribing signals from ships that never answered back. They write science fiction about people who carry messages they were never meant to open.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A routine haul between two silent stations establishes his isolation, his failing human-language dreams, and the war's quiet strangulation of the route. Emotional beat: loneliness mistaken for safety.

chapters.title: A Voice in Dead Air
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. During a sleepless watch he intercepts a repeating distress signal in Ashkari, a language extinct for two centuries—one he somehow half-understands. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: What the Dictionary Forgot
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, with flashbacks to his grandmother's forbidden lullabies. He deciphers fragments and realizes the signal predates the extinction date. Emotional beat: grief for a heritage he denied.

chapters.title: Cargo That Breathes
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. At Waypoint Nine he quietly asks old contacts about Ashkari; word spreads faster than intended. Introduce Iyo, a disgraced medic, and Tetch, a teenage stowaway mechanic. Emotional beat: first fragile trust.

chapters.title: The Hunter's Wake
chapters.summary: Veyran officer Sarel Dannek's POV. She is ordered to intercept any vessel carrying 'linguistic contraband' and begins tracking the Long Silence. Emotional beat: duty shadowed by doubt.

chapters.title: Running Dark
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The Long Silence goes dark through the Cinder Drift to evade Dannek; Tetch proves indispensable in the engine room. Emotional beat: found family forming under pressure.

chapters.title: The Courier's Price
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. His trusted relay contact sells his position to the Kessian government, revealing the treaty's existence is already known. Emotional beat: betrayal by the only law he respected.

chapters.title: Ashkar Remembers
chapters.summary: Iyo's POV. She tends Mara after an injury and hears him speak Ashkari in his sleep—fluently. She confronts him gently. Emotional beat: identity surfacing against his will.

chapters.title: Two Flags, One Prison
chapters.summary: Dannek's POV. She captures a Kessian courier ship carrying forged counter-evidence and realizes both governments are manufacturing lies. Emotional beat: her certainty cracks.

chapters.title: The Station of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The crew shelters at a neutral station run by exiles of every faction; an Ashkari elder recognizes Mara's dream-speech as the true dialect. Emotional beat: belonging he cannot refuse.

chapters.title: Dreaming in the Old Tongue
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Guided by the elder, Mara re-enters his suppressed dreams and recovers the full treaty context—the Ashkari survived, hidden, and their message names war criminals on both sides. Emotional beat: terror and homecoming at once.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Dannek's POV. Her hunter corners the station; she demands the message but hesitates when she hears it broadcast openly among refugees. Emotional beat: conscience over orders.

chapters.title: The Deal Nobody Signed
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A Kessian agent offers Mara amnesty and wealth to hand over the treaty quietly; Tetch overhears and feels betrayed before understanding. Emotional beat: temptation and repair.

chapters.title: Burn the Map
chapters.summary: Tetch's POV. The crew scatters false trails across three systems while copying the treaty to every independent relay they can reach. Emotional beat: loyalty as action, not words.

chapters.title: Sarel's Choice
chapters.summary: Dannek's POV. Ordered to destroy the station regardless of civilians, she refuses, feeds her fleet false coordinates, and defects toward the Long Silence. Emotional beat: justice chosen over law.

chapters.title: The Weight of Words
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. With Dannek aboard and both fleets converging, Mara must decide where to broadcast from—and accept that doing so paints a target on everyone he loves. Emotional beat: responsibility embraced.

chapters.title: Neutral Ground
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. The crew reaches the derelict Ashkari beacon at the war's original flashpoint, the one place both fleets hesitate to fire first. Emotional beat: held breath.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Under fire, Mara transmits the treaty in Ashkari, Kessian, and Veyran simultaneously, authenticating it with living speech no archive can fake. The Long Silence is crippled. Emotional beat: sacrifice as testimony.

chapters.title: Ceasefire, Unofficial
chapters.summary: Dannek's POV. Her former fleet stands down rather than fire on the beacon; soldiers on both sides begin refusing orders as the truth spreads. Emotional beat: the war ending one conscience at a time.

chapters.title: What Survives Extinction
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Rescued from the wreck, Mara meets the living Ashkari community the signal came from and speaks with them face to face. Emotional beat: identity no longer a wound but a door.

chapters.title: The Table Without Thrones
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Months later, negotiations convene on neutral ground with Ashkari witnesses; Mara serves as translator, refusing to let either side soften the record. Emotional beat: justice as ongoing work.

chapters.title: Dreams in Every Language
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, closing. Aboard a new small ship—with Iyo, Tetch, and Dannek choosing to stay—Mara dreams again, this time in many tongues at once. Emotional beat: peace earned, family kept, journey continuing.
